summary: repeat constructs a new string by concatenating the receiver the requested number of times.
documentation: repeat constructs a new string by concatenating the receiver the requested number of times. Zero produces an empty string. Negative or infinite counts raise RangeError.
inputs: A repetition count, converted to an integer.
caution: Large counts can allocate too much memory. This exercise bounds the count; repetition is not a substitute for a safe rendering limit.
scenarios: Generate a short plain-text progress marker.
Build a fixed-width separator in a receipt preview.
Repeat a template fragment in a bounded local display.
title: Build a progress marker
problem: Input is an integer from 0 through 20. Return that many # characters as one string, with no spaces.
goal: Use String.repeat() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Repeat the one-character string # by the input count.
